author: val
body: The canvas is at (50,30) and the pan is (7,-3), neither at the origin and neither symmetric, because a canvas at 0,0 with pan 0 hides an origin bug: every term that should be added would read the same as one that is missing. The same lesson cost this lane a reading on the layout engine, where a container at (50,30) is what made the cursor-starts-at-zero sabotage fire.

author: val
body: Round-trips are pinned at zoom 100 only, and that is deliberate rather than lazy. Above 100 the transforms divide by 100 one way and multiply the other, so truncation legitimately loses sub-unit precision and a round-trip row would pin an artefact instead of a contract. The negative row is there because a transform that dropped a sign or clamped at zero would still pass on positives alone.

author: val
body: The snap-negative row is the assertion; the other twelve rows are its controls. Sabotage measured 2026-07-28 against seed 7C2FF75D: restoring the truncating form ((val + half) / grid) * grid moves ONLY `snap neg` (to -9=0 -10=0 -25=0 -35=-20) and leaves origin, pan, all four round-trips, both zoom ladders, fit, contains, snap-pos and snap-g0 untouched. A one-row sabotage on a thirteen-row test is what says the test discriminates rather than merely covers.

author: val
body: Both zoom ladders are run past their clamp on purpose: sixteen zoom-in steps to reach 800 and stay there, ten zoom-out steps to reach 10 and stay there. A ladder stopped one step short would pass against a clamp that does not exist. The snap grid-zero row pins the divide-by-zero guard, which is the one arm of this function no coordinate value can reach.
